p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.1: The whole model in one picture
p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.2: The pieces from the last few slides, together:
p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.3: Embedding turns ids into vectors: x [T, 4096].
p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.4: The residual stream is the vertical orange line: x, which comes along the whole way.
p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.5: One block (the dashed box) reads the stream twice, via a normalized copy, and adds two contributions. First attention, then the MLP.
p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.6: The block repeats 32 times with new weights. The shape never changes.
p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.7: The final RMSNorm normalizes the stream a single time, and the LM head turns it into one number per token in the vocabulary.
p3.hela-modellen-i-en-bild.8: The rest of the module opens the dashed box and goes through each part.
p3.residual-stream.2: Every token has a vector of 4096 numbers that travels through the whole model. It is called the residual stream, and we write it x.
p3.residual-stream.3: Think of it as one notepad per token. Every block in the model reads the notepad, works out a short note and adds it. Nothing erases what is already written there.
p3.residual-stream.4:
x = embedding
x = x + contribution from block 1
x = x + contribution from block 2
…
p3.residual-stream.5: The name comes from the residual connection: each block only produces a correction, a remainder, that is added on top. The path straight through, where x passes unchanged, always remains.
p3.residual-stream.6: That gives three benefits: information from early blocks survives to the end, deep models train stably, and the stream becomes the natural place to measure and steer the model.
p3.residual-stream.9: 8 dimensions instead of 4096. The outline shows the most recent contribution.
p3.rmsnorm.2: The normalization scales each token’s vector so that its RMS becomes 1, then multiplies by a learned weight per dimension:
p3.rmsnorm.3:
rms = sqrt(mean(x²) + ε)        per token
y   = x / rms ⊙ g

x [T, 4096] → y [T, 4096]
g [4096]   (learned, one per dimension)
p3.rmsnorm.4: Without normalization the stream would grow in size layer by layer, since everything is added. Attention and the MLP want their input at a stable scale.
p3.rmsnorm.5: RMSNorm is a simplified LayerNorm: no mean subtraction and no bias. Cheaper, and works just as well.
p3.rmsnorm.6: Division by the RMS preserves the direction and sets the size. The learned weight g then scales each dimension separately, so the direction shifts a little, but the same shift applies to every token, and that is why directions in the stream remain meaningful and comparable.
p3.attention-1-q-k-och-v.2: Every token makes three different versions of its vector: a question, a label and some content. This happens with three learned matrices.
p3.attention-1-q-k-och-v.3: The normalized stream is projected into three new tensors:
p3.attention-1-q-k-och-v.4: Query: what this position is looking for
p3.attention-1-q-k-och-v.6: Value: what it passes on if it is chosen
p3.attention-1-q-k-och-v.7: K and V are narrower than Q because Llama-3-8B uses GQA: 8 KV heads versus 32 query heads.
p3.attention-1-q-k-och-v.8: vLLM merges the three matrices into a single qkv_proj and splits the result afterwards. One big matmul is faster than three small ones.
p3.attention-1-q-k-och-v.18: The rectangles are to scale: width = columns, height = rows (T = 5).
p3.attention-2-dela-upp-i-heads.2: Instead of one big question, each token asks 32 smaller questions at once, so it can look for several different things at the same time.
p3.attention-2-dela-upp-i-heads.3: Q is split into 32 separate query vectors of 128 dimensions. They are computed from the same token representation and are not guaranteed to be statistically independent. A reshape makes the split explicit without moving data.
p3.attention-2-dela-upp-i-heads.5: Each head runs its own attention in parallel and can learn to look for different things: the previous token, references, matching brackets.
p3.attention-3-rope.2: Attention does not in itself know which word came first. RoPE rotates queries and keys by position, so that the distance between the words shows up.
p3.attention-3-rope.3: Attention itself knows nothing about order. Llama rotates Q and K by position before they are compared (Rotary Position Embedding).
p3.attention-3-rope.4: Each head vector of 128 dimensions is seen as 64 pairs. Pair i is rotated by the angle pos · θᵢ:
p3.attention-3-rope.5:
θᵢ = base^(−2i / d_h)
base = 500 000 in Llama 3
q'(m) = R(m·θ) q
k'(n) = R(n·θ) k
q'(m) · k'(n) depends only on (m − n)
p3.attention-3-rope.6: Early pairs rotate quickly and capture proximity. Late pairs rotate slowly and distinguish long distances.
p3.attention-3-rope.7: The shapes do not change. RoPE is applied to Q and K, never V, and K is stored rotated in the KV cache.
p3.attention-4-scores-och.1: Attention 4: scores and the causal mask
p3.attention-4-scores-och.2: Here each query is compared with every earlier label. The result is a table that says how much each word should listen to every other one.
p3.attention-4-scores-och.3: Each query is compared with every key via the dot product. That gives one matrix per head:
p3.attention-4-scores-och.4:
S = Q Kᵀ / √d_h
[32, T, 128] @ [32, 128, T] → [32, T, T]
S[i, j] = −∞  if j > i     (causal mask)
P = softmax(S, row by row)
p3.attention-4-scores-och.5: With GQA, 4 query heads share the same K: heads 0–3 use KV head 0, heads 4–7 use KV head 1, and so on.
p3.attention-4-scores-och.6: The mask means position i only sees positions 0..i. That is what makes the model autoregressive, and it is why K and V for old positions never change.
p3.attention-4-scores-och.7: S is T × T. At 32,000 tokens that is a billion numbers per head and layer. FlashAttention therefore computes in blocks and never writes the whole matrix to memory.
p3.attention-5-hamta-values.1: Attention 5: fetch values and write back
p3.attention-5-hamta-values.2: Each token takes a mix of the contents it chose to listen to, and adds the mix to its own vector.
p3.attention-5-hamta-values.3: The weights in P are used to mix the values:
p3.attention-5-hamta-values.4:
O = P V
[32, T, T] @ [32, T, 128] → [32, T, 128]
→ transpose/reshape → [T, 4096]
out = O @ Wo     Wo [4096, 4096]
x = x + out
p3.attention-5-hamta-values.5: Each token’s output is a weighted sum of the values of earlier tokens. Wo mixes the results from all the heads and writes to the stream.
p3.attention-5-hamta-values.6: Click a word in the demonstration. The weights are hand-picked to show the idea, not taken from a real model.
p3.gqa-delade-kv-heads.2: In classic Multi-Head Attention, every query head has its own K and V. Grouped-Query Attention lets a group of query heads share one KV pair.
p3.gqa-delade-kv-heads.3: Quality is affected only slightly, but the KV cache shrinks by a factor of n_h / n_kv. For Llama-3-8B the cache is 4 times smaller, which leaves room for 4 times as many concurrent sequences.
p3.mlp-med-swiglu.2: Now each token is processed on its own: the vector is blown up, the patterns that fit are let through, and the result is squeezed back together.
p3.mlp-med-swiglu.3:
h    = RMSNorm(x)            [T, 4096]
gate = h @ W_gate           [T, 14336]
up   = h @ W_up             [T, 14336]
a    = SiLU(gate) ⊙ up      [T, 14336]
out  = a @ W_down           [T, 4096]
x    = x + out
p3.mlp-med-swiglu.4: The MLP works on every token independently. It expands to 3.5 times the width, lets a gate decide which of the 14,336 neurons are let through, and compresses back.
p3.mlp-med-swiglu.5: SiLU(z) = z · σ(z) is a soft ReLU. The gate is multiplied element-wise by up, so each neuron is “a detector times a value”.
p3.mlp-med-swiglu.6: vLLM merges W_gate and W_up into one gate_up_proj [4096, 28672].
p3.var-parametrarna-finns.19: More than two thirds of the model is the MLP. The attention weights are few, but the attention computation grows with the context length.
p3.var-parametrarna-finns.20: Memory for the weights in bf16 (2 bytes per parameter): 8.03 B × 2 ≈ 16 GB. That is the number that decides which GPU you need, before the KV cache is even counted.
p3.spara-tensorerna-genom.1: Trace the tensors through the model
p3.spara-tensorerna-genom.2: Click through a forward pass. Switch between prefill (the whole prompt at once) and decode (one new token with the KV cache).
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.2: What shape do the attention scores have in one layer when prefilling 1000 tokens in Llama-3-8B?
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.3: [32, 1000, 1000] per sequence: one T × T matrix per query head.
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.4: Why do K and V never change for an old position when new tokens arrive?
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.5: Causal mask: position i only sees 0..i. Everything that affects K and V for position i, including all earlier layers, depends only on tokens 0..i. That is why they can be stored, which is the whole idea behind the KV cache.
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.6: Where are most of the parameters, in attention or in the MLP?
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.7: MLP: 176 M per layer versus 42 M for attention in Llama-3-8B.
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.8: What is the difference between n_h and n_kv, and what does it affect?
p3.testa-dig-sjalv.9: n_h is the number of query heads (32), n_kv the number of KV heads (8). The ratio 4 determines how many query heads share the same K and V, and how much smaller the KV cache becomes compared with MHA.
